title: GM Aims to Bring ‘Eyes-Off’ Driving to AI-Powered Cars Within 2 Years
partialText: General Motors is seeking help from artificial intelligence to keep up with Chinese companies that introduce vehicles very quickly.

title: U.S. to Tap Heating Oil Reserves Ahead of Midterm Elections
partialText: The Trump administration will release 315,000 barrels of heating oil, but analysts say the amount is too small to make much of a difference.

title: France Riots Expose the Rage Aimed at Dior, Hermès and Other Luxury Brands
partialText: The looting of stores belonging to brands like Dior, Celine and Hermès has exposed a crack in the glossy facade.

title: Alaska’s Journalists Join Forces to Cover the Midterms
partialText: The state’s challenging geography and newspapers’ broader economic struggles have stretched reporters in Alaska, just as its competitive U.S. Senate race has grabbed national attention.

title: How The New York Times Reports on A.I. Images
partialText: A Times reporter and editors discuss the challenges of sifting through what’s real and what’s not in pursuit of the news.

title: SpaceX Boosts the A.I. Rally
partialText: Tech stocks are up after the rocket and artificial intelligence company beat earnings estimates — and Elon Musk confirmed it is weighing a deal with Tesla.

partialText: A deal would consolidate Elon Musk’s holdings in rockets, cars and artificial intelligence into a company worth well over $3 trillion.

title: Senator Asks 4 Accounting Giants to Describe Malta Tax Advice
partialText: Ron Wyden, ranking Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, is investigating the firms over their role in helping corporations dodge billions in taxes.

title: A Battle for Control of India’s Biggest Business Empire
partialText: A boardroom fight, an attempted veto and government intervention have plunged the Tata Group, one of India’s most revered institutions, into a fight over its future.

title: For an Experiment in Political Affirmative Action, Look to Taiwan
partialText: The island adopted quotas for women running for public office decades before other countries. The upshot? Today, few of them need quotas to get elected.

title: U.K. Approves Long-Stalled Jackdaw Gas Drilling Project in the North Sea
partialText: The project will lessen the country’s dependence on imported energy, though environmental advocates say it undercuts a pledge to reduce carbon emissions.

title: Britain Is Said to Approve New Gas Drilling in the North Sea
partialText: Jackdaw, a natural gas field off the coast of Scotland, would be the first new gas extraction project in the North Sea since a government moratorium in 2024.

title: SpaceX Swings to a Profit, as A.I. Business Grows
partialText: Elon Musk’s rocket company said its artificial intelligence spending had soared, but revenue more than doubled from its Starlink internet satellite service and A.I. products.

title: Netflix Is Great at Making Money. Its Problem Is Keeping Viewers Hooked.
partialText: The streaming service reported a 12 percent increase in quarterly revenue, but acknowledged that stagnant viewership, particularly in the U.S. and Canada, was a major concern.

title: Boeing’s Large 737 Max Jet Secures U.S. Approval
partialText: After years of delay, the Federal Aviation Administration certified the 737 Max 10, the largest version of Boeing’s most popular plane.

title: Heading to France? Amid Recent Unrest, Here’s What to Know
partialText: Rioting over affordability and public education has swept through Paris and other French cities, and there may be more to come.

title: Trump Tariffs on Canada Spark Latest Lawsuit Over Trade Powers
partialText: Once again, the president’s ability to wage a trade war without Congress will come before a court that has repeatedly ruled against him.

title: A ‘Doom Loop’ Threatens France as Populism Confronts Markets
partialText: The turmoil shows the profound challenges facing governments stuck between unhappy citizens and wary bond investors.

title: Investors in Anticipation Over Musk’s Next Big SpaceX Deal
partialText: Ahead of SpaceX’s quarterly earnings report, many on Wall Street are wondering whether Elon Musk will combine it with Tesla.

title: Trump Announces $8 Billion Plan to Cover Farm Losses
partialText: Under the Harvest Fuel Relief Program, the Agriculture Department will provide economic aid for farmers hurt by high diesel prices.

title: Knicks Ticket Prices Are Soaring After Last Season’s Championship
partialText: Knicks tickets have never been cheap, but prices for the first game alone are soaring after last season’s championship — more than a trip to Paris.

title: How Do Airports Prepare for a Plane Crash? Go Inside JFK’s Disaster Drill.
partialText: U.S. airports are required to hold a full-scale disaster drill every three years. Go inside a simulated plane crash at Kennedy Airport last weekend.

title: Christiane Amanpour Says She Is Leaving CNN After 43 Years
partialText: The chief international anchor, one of the most famous names in broadcast news, started as an assistant at the network in 1983.

title: Jon Stewart to Stay at ‘The Daily Show’ Through the 2028 Election
partialText: Ratings have surged since Mr. Stewart returned over two years ago to host the show on Monday nights.

title: Saudi Arabia Postpones Its FII Investment Event After Houthi Attacks
partialText: The Future Investment Initiative, a centerpiece of Saudi efforts to diversify its economy from its reliance on the energy industry, was set to begin next week.

title: Black Unemployment Hints at a Job Market in Worse Shape Than It Seems
partialText: The Black unemployment rate climbed a percentage point to 7 percent in September, almost double the rate for white workers.

title: Gilbert Bigio, Haitian Tycoon Linked to Gangs, Dies at 91
partialText: Reportedly the wealthiest man in the poorest country in the Western Hemisphere, Gilbert Bigio was sanctioned for ties to criminal gangs. He was 91.

title: At Victoria’s Secret’s 2026 Fashion Show, an Old Stereotype of Sexy
partialText: The angels were out in full force on the runway, including Kylie Jenner and both Hadids. So were the wings.

title: Elon Musk Says He Will Give a SpaceX Share to ‘Every Kid in America’
partialText: Anthropic, an A.I. rival to SpaceX, earlier said it would form a “public benefit fund” and other tech moguls have contributed to savings accounts for children.

partialText: The artificial intelligence giant plans to contribute 5 percent of its stock into a philanthropic fund. But its generosity depends on the A.I. boom continuing.

title: Art Basel Las Vegas? The Fight Over Miami Beach’s Fair
partialText: After 18 months of negotiations and warnings that it might relocate to Nevada, the Art Basel fair will remain in Miami Beach through 2031.

title: ‘A Ticking Time Bomb’: An Economic Crisis Looms in Indonesia

title: U.S. Political Money Funnels to Indian Bots to Lure Voters
partialText: At least three dozen videos of people on the street expressing support for a Democratic candidate appeared millions of times on social media. It was unclear who paid for them.

title: The VW Bus, Now Electrified, Keeps on Truckin’

title: Strong Exports Stabilize China’s Economic Growth in Official Statistics
partialText: A prolonged housing crash, sluggish consumer spending and plunging investment have left China dependent on exports to keep the economy growing.

title: Elizabeth Holmes Documentary ‘You Can See Everything’ Opens to Over 2,000 Sold-Out Shows
partialText: “You Can See Everything,” a documentary about the Theranos founder, made a big splash for a movie not yet in wide release. And Netflix had a box office milestone.

title: 3 Charts That Explain the Economy as Voters Head to the Polls
partialText: Inflation is high, consumer spending is strong and seemingly everything depends on what happens with artificial intelligence.

title: Oklahoma Families Faced the Hottest Summer Ever and an Electricity Crisis
partialText: Record heat and a rising demand for electricity are closing in on Oklahoma families trying to keep the lights on and the AC running.

title: United’s C.E.O. Says It Should Cost More Not to Sit in the Middle Seat

title: Trump Offers Putin Economic Relief in Hopes That Russia Will Return the Favor

title: U.S. Budget Deficit Nears $2 Trillion, a Reality Check for Trump’s Cost Cutting
partialText: Higher interest rates are inflating borrowing costs as the Trump administration spends on the Iran war and tariff refunds.

title: You’ve Found a Long-Lost CD. Can You Still Get Your Money?
